title: Prevent human-input decisions from appearing agent-ready
description:
Configure the local Beads workflow so issues labelled decision-needed or human-input never appear in the autonomous ready queue while remaining visible and actionable to the project owner. Advisory epic notes are insufficient protection against agents guessing policy.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the current public surface or workflow described above and observe the stated boundary or gate failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: `br ready` excludes every open decision-needed or human-input issue without hiding it from normal list, show, graph, or owner workflows; automated tests or a repeatable validation command prove the filter; normal implementation beads become ready when all decision dependencies are actually closed.

title: Converge Omnirepo on its Constitution
description:
## Goal

Bring the current 0.8.x implementation into complete alignment with the ratified Omnirepo Constitution and routed Canon architecture.

## Current state

The quality baseline passes, but the product still exposes general repository creation, tag cloning, arbitrary shell execution, and ad hoc synchronization authority. It lacks canonical machine/source/repository configuration, source materialization, exact partials, contained atomic file transactions, verified scoped Git delivery, crash-recoverable durable accounting, bounded repair, and lawful release handling.

## Program rule

Decision-needed children are owner blockers and may not be guessed. Implementation preserves exact one-way authority, visible whole/section edges, independent outcomes, complete durable accounting, bounded sync-induced repair, and the constitutional limits. Actionable migration guidance is mandatory for breaking releases; an automated migrator is implemented only under its explicit decision.

## Success Criteria

See structured acceptance criteria; every mandatory child must close before the epic is eligible.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed; the final implementation passes the Constitution gate across the full product surface; Cargo quality, MSRV, coverage, and pre-commit gates pass; public docs describe only the constitutional product.
notes: Decision-needed and human-input children are policy blockers for the project owner. Agents may audit or prepare questions but must not implement or close them by guessing. Work from dependency-ready implementation beads only. Standalone optional-growth and repository-workflow beads remain visible but are not evidence of an owner decision.

title: Remove the arbitrary multi-repository run surface
description:
Boundary 1 forbids a general repository orchestrator. The public run command and src/run/runners.rs accept arbitrary shell strings and execute sh -c across repositories. Remove only this public and general runner surface, its tests, docs, verbose/global logging coupled to it, and any equivalent arbitrary fleet command. The repository-declared verifier is owned separately and must not be implemented here.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the current public surface or workflow described above and observe the stated boundary or gate failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: omnirepo help no longer advertises run; clap rejects it; no production API accepts an arbitrary user-supplied fleet command; general runner, obsolete tests, docs, and misleading logger help are removed; no replacement general command is introduced; Canon quality gates pass.

title: Orchestrate independent per-repository lifecycle and complete outcomes
description:
Compose immutable plans, contained file transactions, repository verification, operation-scoped Git delivery, durable event emission, scheduler admission, leases and outcome collection. Initial destination passes proceed independently under configured bounded parallelism; completion order is unspecified; one final typed outcome is retained for every fleet member before the separate repair phase.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Each declared repository yields exactly one recoverable outcome covering plan, transaction, check, commit and push stages; valid peers finish despite bounded failures or hangs; changed repositories reach Git only after frozen checks pass; unchanged repositories avoid Git mutation; every typed failure and cancellation retains residue and evidence under policy; events precede effects and completion order never changes accounting.

title: Write complete durable run summaries with quiet success output
description:
Establish the durable run journal before repository mutation, then finalize the decided stable run model and render only its concise terminal projection. Persist run-level preflight and typed lifecycle events under one canonical run and repository identity; concurrent workers emit through the bounded event sink rather than writing terminal output directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Empty, preflight-failed, partial, cancelled, recovered, and successful invocations create one collision-safe record at the canonical path before destination mutation; every selected repository, including queued or interrupted members, reaches one terminal state; checkpoints, corrupt tails, concurrent timestamps, permissions, redaction, evidence bounds, finalization and write failure match policy; terminal output follows the CLI contract with no interleaved progress chatter.

title: Implement the bounded post-pass agent-assisted repair phase
description:
After the initial fleet pass completes, invoke a separate bounded repair subsystem only for failures proven eligible under the current run and repository lineage. Freeze the original source snapshots, synchronization plan, repository policy, checks, and Git preconditions. Reserve attempts durably before agent spawn, enforce confinement outside prompts, then reapply synchronization and rerun original verification before operation-scoped Git delivery.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Pre-sync evidence distinguishes introduced from pre-existing failure under the owner rule; uncertainty or unrelated failure makes no repair change; attempts, incomplete attempts, crashes, timeouts, fallback, restart and exhaustion are durably counted; forbidden, partial, concurrent, and late agent deltas are refused or restored under policy; every accepted attempt is recorded, re-synced and reverified; peers remain independent and exactly one final repository outcome incorporates repair.

title: Implement explicitly delegated breaking migration operation
description:
Implement the owner-decided declared migration artifact and separately invoked migration operation. Migration begins only after explicit delegation, selects an ordered version-applicable chain, uses shared confined agent and lifecycle infrastructure without repair-causation eligibility, and follows decided verification, operation-scoped Git delivery, durable checkpoint, idempotence, interruption, and partial-failure behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Exact installed and predecessor versions are checked before mutation; skipped, already-current, repeat, downgrade, future, unsupported, ambiguous, interrupted and resumed cases follow policy; a real supported 0.8.3 fixture reaches the new version idempotently; machine fleet membership, authoritative source content, source priority and unrelated maintenance remain protected; each destination is durably verified and delivered or reported failed.

title: Align CLI, package metadata, and docs with constitutional synchronization
description:
After the machine-driven CLI and release or migration behavior land, align help, README, CHANGELOG, package metadata and contents, public library surface, examples, setup, installation, and migration guidance with authoritative file and section synchronization. Inventory every user-visible compatibility break since the last actually published supported baseline.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Public wording and package contents describe only constitutional synchronization; legacy commands, ad hoc source authority, .omni.yaml and generic-manager claims are gone; clean-HOME setup reaches first inferred sync; help documents exit, stream, cancellation and record contracts; every removed command, option, schema, side effect, delimiter and public library break has before-and-after guidance and exact migration invocation where provided; changelog links, package audit and supported install procedures pass.

title: Remove the legacy tag-based clone workflow
description:
Remove the public legacy clone --tags workflow and central .omni.yaml generation. This bead is pure removal of tag-driven destination fleet orchestration, its tests, and docs. It does not retain, redesign, or promise source materialization; the separate source policy and catalog beads own any future internal acquisition.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the current public surface or workflow described above and observe the stated boundary or gate failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Public help and APIs expose no tag-driven clone; tag matching cannot determine fleet membership or applicability; .omni.yaml is not generated; legacy implementation, tests, and docs are removed without introducing replacement cloning behavior; Canon quality gates pass.

title: Define source-repository materialization policy
description:
Owner decision required for materializing machine-declared authoritative source repositories. Select supported source-reference classes, revision selection, refresh and cache placement, dirty-source handling, offline and unavailable-priority-source behavior, timeout, retry, cleanup and redaction. For each selected remote class only, decide authentication, ambient Git configuration and URL rewriting, schemes, redirects, proxy, submodules, LFS, filters and cross-origin credential handling.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines one complete lifecycle for every selected source-reference class, including freshness, revision, cache, concurrency, interrupted staging, offline and failure fan-out; an unavailable higher-priority source is never silently omitted to promote a lower source; irrelevant remote policies are not required for local-only classes; the owning Canon page records durable guarantees.

title: Define ownership and precedence for fleet concurrency controls
description:
Owner decision required for repository parallelism and nested child-work limits. Assign controls to the lawful configuration tier and define precedence, any permitted CLI override, defaults, valid ranges, zero behavior, and per-run versus per-repository scope. Agent discovery, repair budgets, evidence bounds, and command semantics are owned by separate decisions.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner assigns every concurrency and scheduler control, exact precedence, defaults, ranges, zero behavior, override rules and scope; repository policy never gains fleet, source or priority authority; the owning Canon page records the durable rule and scheduler/configuration beads can proceed without Rayon defaults.

title: Define configuration serialization, discovery, and conflict policy
description:
Owner decision required for canonical machine, repository, and source-declaration serialization. Select supported <extension> variants at the constitutionally fixed stems <HOME>/.omnirepo/config.<extension> and destination-root .omnirepo.<extension>, plus source-declaration placement under authoritative sources; define exact-root discovery, HOME-unavailable behavior, non-file and unreadable candidates, multi-format conflicts, unknown fields, destination references, aliases, and legacy .omni.yaml handling.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner selects formats at fixed authority locations, exact discovery and conflict behavior, destination reference and existence behavior, absent versus present-invalid handling, unknown-field policy, aliases and legacy migration error behavior; no arbitrary CLI config substitutes machine authority; configuration-authority Canon records the contract.

title: Define managed-item identity, precedence, and collision semantics
description:
Owner decision required for stable whole-file and section identity and source overlap. Define duplicate declaration keys, path and section identity, earlier-versus-later ordered source winner, collisions among whole files and multiple sections in one destination file, reserved authority targets, and whether repository .omnirepo.<extension> may ever be managed without destroying its independent policy authority. Applicability selection is owned separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines stable identities, duplicate and alias handling, overlap winner, grouping and collision rejection for all whole/section combinations, and protected authority targets; configuration-authority and managed-content Canon record the contract; catalogs and plans can resolve conflicts before mutation.

title: Retire general-purpose repository creation
description:
## Constitutional finding

Growth Directive 5 says to grow through file and section synchronization, "not by expanding into general repository orchestration." Boundary 1 limits Omnirepo to synchronization plus commit, push, checks, and sync-induced repair.

## Current evidence

src/bin/main.rs exposes new; src/new/project_creation.rs creates arbitrary repositories, copies tag-selected templates, and runs git init. README.md presents repository creation as a core product feature.

## Scope

Remove the general new command and its production module, tests, and documentation. Any future onboarding must be a synchronization-specific setup path driven by the constitutional configuration and inference model, not a generic project generator.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the current public surface or workflow described above and observe the stated boundary or gate failure.
acceptance_criteria: The public CLI has no general new command; project creation/template-generation code and obsolete tests are removed; README and package wording no longer claim general project generation; installation-to-first-sync onboarding remains covered by the configuration/inference beads; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Define managed-text encoding and exactness contract
description:
Owner decision required because the current String and HTTP text paths may reject invalid UTF-8 or alter BOM and replacement characters while Canon requires faithful exact text. Select whether the authoritative unit is bytes or a named text encoding, supported encodings, BOM handling, invalid-sequence behavior, and the comparison unit.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines the supported representation and exact comparison semantics, including Unicode, BOM, invalid sequences, and newline preservation; managed-content Canon records the rule; catalog, whole-file, partial-section, and documentation beads adopt it consistently.

title: Define managed-section delimiter grammar and format coverage
description:
Owner decision required before literal public delimiters can be implemented. Select marker grammar and section identity, initial extension-to-comment-syntax registry, extension matching, unknown or extensionless behavior, whitespace matching, line versus block comments, and append separator and newline convention. Canon already requires unmatched, reversed, duplicate and nested delimiter ambiguity to fail without mutation.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner selects exact start and end grammar, section identity, supported format registry, matching rules, unknown-format behavior and append convention; existing Canon ambiguity failures remain unchanged; managed-content Canon records the active syntax and the partial engine can proceed without guessing.

title: Define verification-command execution contract
description:
Owner decision required for repository-declared check process mechanics. Define argv versus shell representation, configured order, working directory, environment, stdin, timeout and cancellation, process-tree termination on every supported platform, stdout and stderr capture protocol, and exit, signal, spawn and timeout classification. Permitted side effects and evidence retention are owned separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines the complete process and finality contract, including no ambient shell assumptions, child and descendant handling, bounded capture protocol and every terminal classification; fleet-lifecycle Canon records it; config schema, verifier and harness can implement the mechanics without guessing side-effect or evidence policy.

title: Define scoped Git mutation and push contract
description:
Owner decision required before Omnirepo may commit or push. Define treatment of pre-existing staged, unstaged, untracked, same-file outside-section and local-commit state; literal scoped staging; non-Git repositories, linked worktrees and submodules; branch/upstream, detached, unborn, ahead, behind and diverged states; identity, message, hooks, signing, authentication, timeout, retry and failure residue. Force publication is unavailable.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines a Git contract that cannot stage, publish or rewrite unrelated work or pre-existing commits; exact OID and ref reconciliation covers local commit, remote acceptance, timeout and restart ambiguity; fleet-lifecycle Canon records it; integration tests cover dirty/index/worktree/submodule/branch/auth/hook/signing and failure matrices.

title: Define run-record schema, evidence, and sensitive-data policy
description:
Owner decision required for the durable timestamped run record itself. Define canonical run identifier and collision-free mapping to <HOME>/.omnirepo/runs/<timestamp>.log, canonical repository identity and display aliases, versioned run/repository state machine, creation before mutation, monotonic checkpoint ordering, truncated-tail and startup recovery, finalization, retention linkage, and process outcome when creation or finalization fails. Evidence security is owned separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines record identity, path mapping, schema/version, repository identity, state transitions, checkpoint and recovery semantics, unique timestamp collision behavior, creation/finalization and write-failure outcomes; CLI, repair and migration reference the same identities; fleet-lifecycle Canon records the contract.

title: Define repair eligibility and durable attempt accounting
description:
Owner decision required for proving a failure was caused by the current synchronization and bounding repair. Define required pre-sync baseline, run and repository lineage, introduced versus pre-existing failure evidence, first-run and uncertainty behavior, attempt-budget ownership and scope, durable reservation, incomplete-attempt consumption, restart and tool-fallback behavior, frozen plan and verification policy, and handling of concurrent or late edits.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines causal eligibility, first-run behavior, baseline evidence, uncertainty, attempt accounting across crashes and fallback, and immutable source/plan/policy/check preconditions; agent discovery and trust are owned separately; fleet-lifecycle Canon records the contract and repair can never rely on an agent's assertion of causation.

title: Define declared migration artifact, release binding, and lifecycle contract
description:
Owner decision required for explicitly delegated migration accompanying breaking releases. Define declaration location, schema, integrity and canonical release identity; exact from/to versions and supported predecessor range; ordered composition for skipped releases; delegation signal; idempotence; already-current, downgrade, future, partial, interrupted and resumed states; destination selection; verification, Git, record and agent use.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines a machine-readable release-bound migration and complete explicitly delegated lifecycle, including protected machine and source authority, no unrelated maintenance, unsupported-version handling and recovery; fleet-lifecycle Canon records it; implementation and real-baseline guidance can proceed without invented version semantics.

title: Define fleet CLI and process outcome contract
description:
Owner decision required for the public machine-driven product surface after legacy orchestration is retired. Define sync and setup surfaces, whether the optional explicit migrator is present, permitted overrides, changed/unchanged/empty/preflight/partial/all-failed/repair/record-failure statuses, stdout and stderr, TTY and non-TTY behavior, optional versioned machine output, signals, queued and active cancellation, and config-independent help/version behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Every invocation class has one stable process status and stream contract; all selected repositories including cancelled/not-started have durable terminal states; routine success is silent or one concise projection as decided; help/version/parse errors cause no config load, run record or repository effect; any machine mode is the same human-accessible surface; unselected JSON, dry-run or preview is not invented.

title: Implement repository-declared verification executor
description:
Implement the internal verifier used only by synchronization and permitted recovery. Execute each repository-owned check under the decided process and side-effect contracts, capture typed bounded evidence, terminate complete process trees across supported platforms, protect authority roots outside prompts, and classify every worktree delta. This is not a public arbitrary runner.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Checks execute in configured order and repository scope with decided cwd, environment, network, stdin, timeout, cancellation and output semantics; spawn, nonzero, signal, timeout, forbidden effect and success are typed; no check weakens frozen policy or leaves an unclassified delta; a failed or hung command cannot suppress peers or the durable record; hostile-command integration tests pass.

title: Implement operation-scoped Git commit and push adapter
description:
Implement Git mutation as a narrow adapter for synchronization, permitted repair, and explicitly delegated migration. Stage only the explicit authorized delta for the current operation, preserve unrelated index and worktree state, verify the staged tree and frozen HEAD immediately before commit, durably record exact OID and ref, and push only that commit without force or incidental publication.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Changed clean-pass operations create an inspectable scoped commit and permitted push; unchanged operations create none; failed checks create no Omnirepo commit or push; unrelated and outside-section state is preserved; local commit, remote acceptance, timeout, crash, HEAD/upstream movement and restart ambiguity reconcile without duplicate or accidental publication; all Git failures are typed and residue matches policy.

title: Implement canonical machine and repository configuration authority
description:
Replace legacy configuration with canonical machine, source-declaration, and destination repository policy. Machine configuration alone owns the fleet, ordered authoritative sources, and assigned fleet controls; repository policy owns only managed applicability and repository verification commands. Snapshot all selected configuration before effects, reject alternate authority and aliases, distinguish absent policy from present-invalid policy, and emit contextual redacted errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Only fixed canonical locations and owner-selected extensions load; machine schema owns fleet and ordered sources, repository schema cannot redefine them; clean HOME and malformed shared authority fail before network, source or destination mutation; present invalid local policy never infers; unknown, duplicate, conflicting, unsupported-version and cross-role identities fail contextually; legacy .omni.yaml and arbitrary --config authority follow explicit migration/error policy; round-trip and invalid fixtures pass.

title: Implement trusted configured agent adapter with fail-closed confinement
description:
Implement deterministic configured agent discovery and structured invocation shared by repair and explicitly delegated migration. Enforce protected roots, data exposure, credentials, environment, process tree, control protocol, resource limits and evidence outside prompts before contact; do not grant agents Git delivery, source, fleet, config or run-record authority.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Only compatible configured tools selected under the trusted-discovery contract run; invocation has no ambient shell ambiguity; forbidden capability or unprovidable confinement fails before contact; independent snapshots and manifests reject forbidden, concurrent, late or forged deltas before lifecycle continuation; prompt injection, hostile repositories, crash, timeout, descendants, oversized output and cross-repository attempts pass adversarial tests.

title: Wire the machine-driven fleet synchronization CLI
description:
Wire the constitutional fleet command. Load and snapshot only canonical machine authority, source revisions and catalogs, repository policies, checks and plans; establish the durable run and leases before mutation; execute the initial independent pass; invoke the bounded post-pass repair subsystem for eligible failures within configured limits; fold all stages into exactly one final outcome per declared destination.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: No arbitrary source or fleet override exists; shared authority preflight failure causes zero destination mutation; missing or invalid machine config never triggers ambient scanning; explicit invalid repository policy fails that destination while peers continue; changed, unchanged, empty, partial, total, cancelled, recovered, repair and record failure cases match the CLI contract; help/version paths are config-independent and side-effect-free.

title: Add final constitutional acceptance suite
description:
Add an epic-level black-box suite proving the completed constitutional product across CLI, configuration authority, source precedence, exact whole and partial synchronization, containment, transactions, independent outcomes, verification, Git, records, crash recovery, bounded repair, agent confinement, release safety, and explicit migration when provided.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The suite rejects legacy orchestration, destination-to-source promotion, inference over explicit policy, semantic editing, outside-fleet mutation, check-caused authority escape, failed-check publication, unbounded repair, hostile-agent control and implicit migration; it covers overlapping runs, kill/restart, ambiguous push, first inferred sync, unavailable priority sources, atomic failure, quiet output and durable identities on every supported MSRV platform; required release artifacts and migration identity agree.

title: Make version and release provenance deterministic and gate publication
description:
Replace the quarantined main-push bump and release race with one owner-decided tag-to-source flow. Bind tag, exact commit, Cargo and binary version, changelog, migration declaration and release name; validate conventional and breaking inputs; run every Canon gate on that exact commit; stage all artifacts before public publication; and repair cog.toml metadata and authority.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the current public surface or workflow described above and observe the stated boundary or gate failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Untagged main pushes cannot publish; equivalent tags on different commits are rejected; one exact commit passes formatting, Clippy, full tests, docs, MSRV, coverage and pre-commit before release; migration declaration and guidance exist for every break; all supported artifacts and smoke tests succeed before a draft becomes public; reruns are idempotent, concurrent release attempts are serialized, and release-authority actions use least privilege and immutable revisions.

title: Unify local and CI coverage gate execution
description:
Coverage thresholds are enforced in CI, but local documented piping and duplicated report commands can mask the cargo llvm-cov exit status or present stale evidence. Provide one authoritative local and CI entry point that preserves the threshold result and report artifacts.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the current public surface or workflow described above and observe the stated boundary or gate failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: One repository-owned coverage command enforces 95 percent lines, 80 percent functions, and 80 percent regions with locked all-target all-feature settings; local and CI call the same gate; report generation cannot replace or mask the threshold exit status; documentation and tests or workflow validation are updated.

title: Define supported platforms, filesystem identity, and path representation
description:
Owner decision required for one path and filesystem identity model across configuration, source catalogs, destination containment, Git, processes, and run records. Select supported operating systems and filesystem classes; path representation; case and Unicode equivalence; separator, prefix, UNC, device, alternate-stream, reserved-name, and non-Unicode behavior where applicable; link, junction, reparse, mount, and hard-link identity; and fail-closed behavior on unsupported filesystems.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines supported platforms and one canonical identity and containment relation, including aliases, links, mounts, non-regular files, unsupported filesystems, and configuration representation; the smallest owning Canon pages record the durable contract; every filesystem-facing implementation and test can use it without host-default assumptions.

title: Define managed-file replacement durability and metadata contract
description:
Owner decision required for replacement behavior beyond textual authority. Decide atomic visibility under interruption or crash, temporary-file placement and cleanup, durability and fsync expectations, parent-directory residue, and preservation, replacement, or rejection behavior for permissions, ownership, ACLs, extended attributes, timestamps, read-only files, hard links, and special files.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner selects complete failure, interruption, durability, cleanup, and metadata behavior for new, changed, and unchanged managed files; managed-content Canon records the guarantee; whole-file and partial-section implementations can share one replacement primitive without inventing filesystem policy.

title: Implement containment-aware atomic managed-file transactions
description:
Implement the common destination-file transaction used by whole-file and partial-section synchronization. Resolve all planned changes to one file, verify containment and file identity, compare exact authoritative content, and publish through the decided durability and metadata contract without exposing truncation or following an unsafe alias.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: A transaction produces either the complete authorized new file or the prior file under every injected failure; unchanged content performs no replacement; multiple managed sections in one file are applied once without touching outside content; intervening edits, aliases, hard links, special files, permission failures, ENOSPC, and crash points yield typed outcomes and never mutate outside the destination authority root.

title: Define interruption, recovery, and overlapping-run contract
description:
Owner decision required for process overlap and death. Define canonical run and repository identity, admission and lease scope, ordering and wait-or-fail behavior, stale-owner proof, PID reuse, signals and cancellation, queued and in-flight classification, resume versus terminalize-and-rerun, frozen source/plan/check/HEAD preconditions, crash states around sync, check, commit, push, repair and migration, record failures, ambiguous remote acceptance, and whether explicit delegation survives restart.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines every overlap, interruption, restart, stale-lease, cancellation, ambiguous-effect, and final-outcome case while preserving independent progress for disjoint repositories; fleet-lifecycle Canon records the durable contract; coordination and recovery can be implemented without guessing resume, retry, or lock semantics.

title: Implement crash-recoverable run coordination and repository leases
description:
Implement durable run admission, per-repository exclusion, monotonic lifecycle checkpoints, cancellation, stale-owner recovery, and restart reconciliation under the decided contract. Disjoint repositories remain concurrent while one canonical destination can never undergo overlapping sync, verification, agent, or Git mutation.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Durable intent exists before the first repository mutation; every selected repository reaches a recoverable terminal state; kill points at every lifecycle boundary, two independent processes, stale PID reuse, corrupt or truncated journal tails, ambiguous push acceptance, orphan children, and restart are reconciled without duplicate commits, pushes, agent attempts, or omitted outcomes.

title: Load source-repository declarations with deterministic precedence
description:
Materialize the ordered source snapshots, load their owner-decided declarations, validate and extract authoritative content, and build one immutable catalog with provenance. Resolve duplicate identities and overlapping whole/section targets only by declared source order and collision policy. Complete acquisition and catalog validation before any destination mutation.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Every catalog entry carries source identity, pinned revision, declaration identity, extraction provenance and exact content; unavailable or invalid sources are neither dropped nor reordered; duplicate and overlap resolution follows the owner contract; source mutation during acquisition or catalog load fails preflight; source and destination roles cannot reverse; malformed declarations name source and entry; deterministic catalog fixtures pass.

title: Define source declaration and authoritative content extraction schema
description:
Owner decision required for the records that authoritative source repositories expose. Define required and optional declaration fields; whole-file versus section mode; content locator and relative base; whether section bodies come from bounded source content or separate snippets; source-to-destination path mapping; section reference; applicability metadata; duplicate keys; missing and non-regular content; provenance; and validation.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner supplies a complete machine-readable declaration and extraction contract for whole files and sections that preserves exact content, makes authority edges visible, and confines source reads; configuration-authority and managed-content Canon record it; catalog fixtures can express every valid and invalid item without inferred fields.

title: Define configuration schema evolution and compatibility contract
description:
Owner decision required for evolving machine, source, and repository configuration. Decide schema version representation; absent, old, future, and mixed versions; compatibility window; unknown and deprecated fields; semantic reinterpretation prohibition; break detection; and the relationship between unsupported configuration and actionable or automated migration.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Every supported and unsupported version combination has deterministic load, error, and migration behavior; no version silently changes fleet, source, precedence, applicability, command, or delimiter meaning; the active configuration-authority Canon page records the contract and breaking releases satisfy the migration principle.

title: Implement policy-driven immutable source materialization
description:
Implement acquisition, refresh, pinning, caching, and immutable per-run snapshots for machine-declared source repositories under the decided source policy. Isolate staging from destination work, coordinate concurrent materializers, publish only complete snapshots, and expose the exact revision and provenance consumed by catalog loading.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Each run consumes one complete pinned snapshot per ordered source; unavailable or invalid higher-priority sources are never silently omitted; cache, offline, dirty, interrupted refresh, auth, redirect, proxy, URL rewrite, hooks, filters, submodule, LFS, timeout, retry, crash, and concurrent refresh cases follow policy; no source-controlled mechanism gains destination execution authority.

title: Implement phased configuration preflight and actionable diagnostics
description:
Validate shared machine authority and the complete ordered source catalog before destination mutation, then validate explicit repository policy independently per destination so valid peers may continue. Produce aggregated, stable, redacted diagnostics that identify authority tier, canonical path, field or line when available, source, repository, item, and remediation.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed, unknown, duplicate, conflicting, missing, unreadable, non-regular, multi-format, unsupported-version, and alias cases are covered; truly absent repository policy alone may infer; present invalid policy never falls back to inference; shared-authority failure causes zero destination mutation; per-repository failures do not suppress valid peers; diagnostics never echo secrets.

title: Define trusted agent discovery and invocation protocol
description:
Owner decision required for discovering and invoking configured repair and migration agents. Define supported tool identity, version and capability compatibility, canonical executable discovery, PATH and race handling, priority exhaustion and fallback, argv and stdin protocol without ambient shell interpretation, noninteractive behavior, control messages, evidence identity, timeouts, termination, and unsupported or missing-agent outcomes.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines a deterministic, authenticated-enough tool selection and structured invocation protocol with no compatible-agent and mid-run replacement behavior; fleet-lifecycle Canon records it; the adapter can distinguish control from untrusted output and cannot accept a tool's self-asserted success as evidence.

title: Define agent trust, data exposure, credential, and environment policy
description:
Owner decision required for the trust boundary around local or remote coding agents. Treat repository files, AGENTS and CLAUDE instructions, filenames, diffs, checks, migration content, and agent output as untrusted data. Decide what repository and evidence data may be disclosed; environment, credential, SSH, helper and proxy inheritance; network access; control-channel separation; redaction; late writes; and the behavior when confinement cannot be provided.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines permitted data disclosure, credentials and environment, network and process capabilities, protected authorities, control-channel authentication, redaction, and fail-closed behavior when required confinement is unavailable; no rule grants secret-management or general orchestration authority; all agent consumers share the same contract.

title: Add adversarial agent and hostile-repository acceptance matrix
description:
Build black-box adversarial fixtures for the shared agent boundary and repository-controlled data. Exercise hostile AGENTS and CLAUDE text, source declarations, migration content, filenames, diffs, verification output, fake control messages, fake success, credential probing, descendants, post-exit writes, hooks, filters, Git config, URL rewrites, concurrent edits, incompatible agents, crash, timeout, and oversized output.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Tests prove untrusted repository or source content cannot become control instructions, alter machine or source authority, escape the selected destination, access forbidden credentials, forge evidence, commit or push, weaken checks, or continue mutating after finality; every refusal and failure remains durably attributable while valid peers finish.

title: Implement bounded fleet scheduler and backpressured event delivery
description:
Implement the owner-configured repository scheduler rather than relying on the ambient Rayon pool. Bound repository admission, nested process and agent concurrency, result and evidence queues, and event delivery while preserving unspecified completion order, per-repository sequential stages, cancellation, and complete accounting.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Configured limits are respected for repositories and child work; queue and event memory remain bounded under slow sinks and large output; one hung or failing item cannot starve valid peers after policy finality; cancellation classifies queued and active items; deterministic tests prove no oversubscription, deadlock, lost events, or outcome-order dependence.

title: Test supported filesystem platforms on the MSRV
description:
Add a CI matrix and platform-real fixtures for every owner-supported filesystem platform on Rust 1.86. Exercise the selected identity, containment, replacement, metadata, process termination, Git representation, run-record, and lease contracts instead of assuming Linux pathname and signal behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Each supported platform runs complete MSRV tests and documentation tests plus capability-gated filesystem cases for case and Unicode aliases, non-Unicode names where representable, links, junctions or reparse points, mounts, hard links, non-regular files, permissions, metadata, atomic replacement, concurrent leases, and child termination; unsupported behavior fails explicitly.

title: Add large-fleet performance and exhaustion regression suite
description:
Create deterministic 100- to 500-repository scenarios covering planning, source reuse, bounded scheduling, verification, evidence, durable recording, cancellation, and mixed failures. Measure the resource properties that make unattended fleet maintenance viable without turning timing into flaky correctness.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The suite asserts configured active-repository and child-process maxima, bounded queue and evidence growth, one source snapshot and catalog per run, complete stable outcomes under randomized completion, peer progress with stragglers, cancellation finality, and owner-decided exhaustion behavior; benchmark trends are reportable without weakening correctness gates.

title: Build per-repository synchronization plans with explicit scope and inference
description:
For each machine-declared destination, snapshot explicit repository policy or apply owner-decided inference only when policy is truly absent. Resolve applicable source items, all/allow/exclude reasons, precedence and every whole/section collision into a typed plan grouped by destination file before mutation.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Absent policy infers exactly under the applicability truth table; commands-only, omitted selector, empty selector, allow, exclude, unknown IDs and zero items follow decided semantics; present invalid, unreadable, disappearing or replaced policy fails that repository and never infers; all collisions and reserved targets resolve or fail before writes; the plan explains every inclusion/exclusion and is stable under source and config order.

title: Establish typed core plans, outcomes, and injected adapters
description:
Refactor toward a deterministic core that consumes immutable configuration and source snapshots, resolves typed plans, groups destination-file transactions, and emits typed lifecycle events and outcomes. Isolate filesystem, process, Git, agent, clock, network, and persistence effects behind injected adapters; remove global configuration and presentation coupling.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Core planning and state transitions are testable without ambient HOME, PATH, network, Git, terminal, clock, or filesystem; adapters expose typed bounded failures; one immutable run context carries source revisions, policy snapshots, plan identities, and canonical repository identity; CLI and renderers are projections rather than authority.

title: Remove the legacy ad hoc synchronization source surface
description:
Boundary 2 requires one-way machine-declared source authority. Remove the public legacy sync inputs that accept arbitrary URLs, template IDs, local source files, destination roots, or direct target authority, together with the old reqwest/template resolution path, tests, and documentation. This removal does not implement the replacement fleet command.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the current public surface or workflow described above and observe the stated boundary or gate failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Public help and APIs cannot promote an arbitrary URL, local file, template, or destination repository to authoritative source content; legacy source-selection and central-dir synchronization code, tests, and docs are removed; no hidden compatibility path reverses authority; Canon quality gates pass.

title: Quarantine unsafe main-push tagging and publication
description:
Disable the current independent main-push bump and release paths until the canonical release decision and deterministic publication workflow exist. An ordinary push currently can build one commit and attach its binaries to a different existing version tag. Do not move, delete, or choose among ambiguous existing tags.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the current public surface or workflow described above and observe the stated boundary or gate failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: A normal main push cannot create or move a tag, create a public release, or upload binaries; no mutable external reusable workflow retains tag or release authority; equivalent version tags pointing to different commits are detected and reported without history rewrite; static workflow validation proves untagged commits cannot publish.

title: Define release identity, breaking-change signaling, and distribution contract
description:
Owner decision required for lawful breaking releases. Define canonical version source and tag form, release trigger, source-commit binding, equivalent existing tag handling, pre-1.0 breaking signaling, conventional-commit treatment, supported installation and update channels and targets, and binding between release identity, migration declaration, and actionable guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: One canonical mapping exists among commit, package version, tag, binary version, changelog, release name, and migration identity; invalid and breaking inputs have explicit behavior; supported distribution channels and platforms are named; conflicting existing tags have a non-destructive policy; the smallest owning Canon page records the Principle 8 guarantee.

title: Build verifiable release bundles and upgrade smoke tests
description:
Implement the owner-selected distribution channels and test real install and upgrade artifacts without adding a general updater. Audit the package and each binary bundle, bind them to one release identity, and exercise upgrade from the last actually published supported baseline through explicitly delegated migration.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Clean-tree locked packaging and every supported bundle contain only intentional files and report the canonical version; fresh installation works through each supported channel; a hermetic real 0.8.3 fixture upgrades, migrates, reaches first successful sync, and is idempotent; unsupported predecessor, downgrade, future, partial artifact, and mismatched declaration fail without mutation or publication.

title: Define repository synchronization transaction and failure residue
description:
Owner decision required for the destination worktree state produced by a failed lifecycle. Decide shared versus per-repository preflight, multi-file and multi-section ordering, whether later items continue after one item fails, transaction grouping, temporary and parent-directory residue, rollback versus retained authoritative changes, and the visible worktree and index state after sync, verification, commit, or push failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines every preflight, partial-application, continuation, rollback-or-retain, cleanup, and stage-failure residue case; managed-content and fleet-lifecycle Canon record the durable behavior; lifecycle, whole-file, section, Git, recovery, and tests can assert one unambiguous destination state.

title: Define verification side effects and confinement contract
description:
Owner decision required because repository-declared verification commands may themselves mutate files, spawn descendants, use the network, or reach other authority roots. Decide whether checks are observational, permitted destination-local changes, generated or auto-fixed file treatment, environment and network access, and fail-closed protection of sources, machine config, run records, Git authority, and other repositories.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines permitted verifier effects and how every resulting delta is classified, frozen, reverted, retained, or rejected; sources, machine authority, run evidence, Git authority, and repositories outside the selected destination remain protected; fleet-lifecycle Canon records the rule and verifier tests can enforce it outside command text.

title: Define repository applicability and inference semantics
description:
Owner decision required for choosing which source-declared items apply to one destination. Define absent, present, commands-only, omitted selector, and intentionally empty repository policy; applicability matching; all, allow, and exclude combination truth table; unknown and invalid selectors; target-existence relevance; and zero-item behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner supplies an exhaustive applicability and selection truth table with explainable include and exclude reasons; explicit policy is never mistaken for absence; configuration-authority Canon records the contract; configuration and planner tests cover every branch without inferred defaults.

title: Define run-evidence security, bounds, and retention policy
description:
Owner decision required for verification, Git, source, repair, migration, and agent evidence stored in durable run records. Define per-stream and per-item bounds, binary handling, truncation markers, redaction and URL treatment, permissions, retention and deletion behavior, and which evidence is shown in terminal projections.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner defines evidence classes, limits, truncation, encoding or binary handling, redaction, permissions, retention, deletion, and terminal exposure; fleet-lifecycle Canon records the security contract; producers and the durable writer can reject or bound hostile output without losing final outcome accounting.

title: Implement synchronization-specific setup and diagnostics
description:
Implement a narrow onboarding path to canonical machine configuration, source declaration validation, destination and repository-policy diagnostics, and first inferred synchronization. It may prepare synchronization authority explicitly selected by the user but must not create arbitrary repositories or discover an ambient fleet.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: From a clean HOME, documented setup can create or validate the minimal owner-decided machine configuration and one source declaration, check source and destination reachability without managed-content mutation, explain repository-policy inference and errors, and reach a first inferred sync; no arbitrary repository generator, ambient scan, or general command runner is introduced.

title: Implement idempotent exact whole-file synchronization
description:
Apply whole-file plan entries through the shared contained file transaction. Compare the owner-decided exact representation and replace authoritative content only when different; preserve exact newline, Unicode, BOM and invalid-sequence behavior selected by policy; aggregate repository-local errors while peers continue.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Authoritative exact content creates missing and replaces drifting whole files; an equal target is a true filesystem no-op on every supported platform; LF, CRLF, mixed, final-newline, Unicode, BOM and invalid-sequence cases follow the encoding contract; nested paths and missing targets work; source decode/acquisition failure writes nothing; replacement, metadata, residue and concurrent-edit behavior come from the shared transaction; repeated runs are idempotent.

title: Implement managed partial sections and delimiter knowledge
description:
Implement the owner-selected comment-syntax registry and managed-section editor on top of the shared contained file transaction. Match literal start and end delimiters and section identity, preserve all content outside every managed span exactly, group multiple sections in one file, append a missing declared section under the decided separator convention, and reject every ambiguity before mutation.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Existing, empty, adjacent and multiple sections converge and repeat as no-ops; prefix, suffix, other sections, CRLF and final-newline state remain exact; marker-like payload substrings are data; unmatched, reversed, interleaved, nested, duplicate or ambiguous delimiters and unknown formats fail contextually with original bytes unchanged; missing file or pair appends exactly by policy; property tests prove only bounded managed spans change.

title: Enforce symlink-safe containment within the declared fleet
description:
Enforce the constitutional authority roots for every operation using the owner-decided filesystem identity model: source reads within pinned source snapshots; destination file, verification, agent and Git effects within the selected destination; machine configuration and durable records within their roots. Replace lexical-only joining with fail-closed no-follow containment resilient to aliases and concurrent swaps.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the current public surface or workflow described above and observe the stated boundary or gate failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Root, intermediate and leaf symlinks plus supported reparse, junction, mount, case, Unicode, separator, hard-link and canonical aliases cannot redirect effects outside authority; relative fields reject absolute, parent and device forms as applicable; config, source, destination, .git and run-record paths are covered; concurrent swap and special-file fixtures fail closed before out-of-root mutation while valid peers finish.

title: Build a hermetic fleet lifecycle integration-test harness
description:
Build schema-neutral hermetic fixtures for the complete fleet lifecycle: isolated HOME, PATH, network and credentials; source snapshots; destination repositories and bare remotes; deterministic clock, run IDs and signals; filesystem fault injection; fake verification, Git and agents; PTY and non-TTY capture; process-tree control; two independent CLI processes; and explicit barriers rather than sleeps.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures reproduce supported filesystem aliases and failures, ENOSPC and permissions, kill points, corrupt journals, stale PID reuse, overlapping invocations, child hangs and descendants, remote-accepted timeout, source refresh interruption, hostile environment and repository data, large bounded output, randomized completion and 100-plus repository runs without ambient network, Git config, proxies, credentials or toolchains.
